title: Acceleration of Graph Neural Networks with Heterogenous Accelerators Architecture
problem: GraphSAGE sampling stage on CPU is a critical bottleneck due to graph data characteristics that do not parallelize efficiently on GPUs alone. GPU acceleration of GNNs is fundamentally limited by CPU-based sampling overhead.
motivation: GNNs are essential for high-impact applications like drug discovery and social media analysis, but achieving practical speedup requires addressing sampling bottlenecks that GPUs cannot efficiently handle.
method: The system uses two specialized processors working together: an FPGA (customizable hardware designed for specific tasks) accelerates the sampling stage—selecting relevant data points from the graph—while the GPU handles neural network training. Graph sampling normally becomes a bottleneck on GPU systems because graph data doesn't parallelize efficiently on standard GPUs, so moving this computation to an FPGA that can handle it better eliminates the slowdown. Sampled data flows directly from FPGA memory to GPU memory through PCIe peer-to-peer communication (a fast direct link between the two chips), bypassing the CPU and avoiding communication overhead. This allows the GPU to focus purely on training while the FPGA continuously feeds it prepared data.
key_novelty: The core innovation is using an FPGA to accelerate graph sampling and connecting it directly to the GPU through PCIe peer-to-peer communication, eliminating the CPU bottleneck that limits GPU-only graph neural network training.
contributions: Profiling and identification of sampling as the critical bottleneck in GraphSAGE
FPGA accelerator design for graph sampling algorithms
Heterogeneous architecture with PCIe P2P communication pipeline between FPGA and GPU
Demonstrated 2.38-8.55× speedup on sampling and 1.24-1.99× end-to-end improvement
limitations: Limitations and scalability analysis not discussed in abstract.
primary_theme: FPGA-GPU heterogeneous acceleration for GNN sampling bottleneck
